title: 0267's fix landed and its diagnostic did not -- the cross-thread refusal is byte-identical to the no-id refusal, and for the cross-thread case its sentence is false
body:
**`0267`'s FIX LANDED AND ITS DIAGNOSTIC DID NOT. THE REFUSAL IS CORRECT AND ITS REASON IS UNSAYABLE FROM THE OUTPUT.**

`at lint` now refuses a citation whose id appears only under another thread's name -- which is `0267`'s fix and it works. **But the message it prints is byte-identical to the message for a file carrying no id at all.**

## Driven, in an isolated scratch project against a debug build at HEAD

One thread, one test-backed criterion, one AT row citing `tests/other.rs`, row green so the citation arm runs. Three file contents, three runs:

| `tests/other.rs` contains | rc | message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `// ST0001 AT-01.1 -- witnesses this thread` | 0 | `ok -- 1 of 1 AT row(s) examined and conforming` |
| `// ST0002 AT-01.1 -- witnesses thread B and nothing else` | 1 | `tests/other.rs does not carry the literal id AT-01.1` |
| `// nothing here names any row` | 1 | `tests/other.rs does not carry the literal id AT-01.1` |

**The second and third rows print the same sentence, and for the second row that sentence is FALSE: the file does carry the literal id `AT-01.1`.** What it does not carry is a line bearing that id which names no other thread -- a different and much narrower fact.

## Why this costs a user real time rather than being cosmetic

**The message sends them to check the one thing that is already true.** A user in the cross-thread case reads *does not carry the literal id*, greps the file, finds `AT-01.1` on line 1, and has every reason to conclude the tool is broken. **Nothing in the output mentions threads, qualification, or the rule that was actually applied**, so the correct next action -- change `ST0002` to the citing thread, or drop the thread qualifier entirely -- is not reachable from what they were told.

**And the ordinary form still counts**, which makes the confusion sharper rather than milder: an unqualified `// AT-01.1` conforms, so the user's mental model of *the id must be present* is CORRECT and the tool appears to contradict it.

## The class

**This is the same shape as `0287` and as `int cli`'s refusal naming a cause it never computed: a check whose verdict is right and whose stated reason describes a different test than the one it ran.** A guard that refuses for reason B while printing reason A is worse than one that prints nothing, because the printed reason is what the user acts on. **The fix is not to the refusal; it is to make the message say which of the two conditions failed.**

## Suggested remedy

Two messages instead of one, both naming the rule. Absent: *`<path>` does not carry the literal id `<AT>`*. Present-but-foreign: *`<path>` carries `<AT>` only on lines naming another thread (`ST0002`); at least one line carrying the id must not name a different thread, and a line naming no thread at all is the ordinary form and counts*. The second sentence already exists as prose in `docs/known-defects.md`; it is not in the tool.

## Provenance

Found while driving every remedy on `docs/known-defects.md` for `AC-02.3`'s declared limit -- the page verifies that a defect is STATED and never that its remedy WORKS. **The `0267` fix itself is confirmed working by this same drive; only its diagnostic is wrong.** Both controls fired: the conforming case and the genuinely-absent case.
